title: Roy Cohn Became Chief Counsel to Senator Joseph McCarthy in 1953
description_medium: Senator Joseph McCarthy hired Roy Cohn in 1953 as chief counsel for the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. PBS reports that McCarthy relied on Cohn for contacts, information, ideas, and political advice during the committee’s work. Cohn’s appointment placed him at the center of a period of congressional investigations associated with the Red Scare, but the sources do not show that he alone invented McCarthyism or connect the appointment to Donald Trump.
description_long: In 1953, Senator Joseph McCarthy hired Roy Cohn as chief counsel to the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. PBS’s American Experience account says McCarthy relied heavily on Cohn for contacts, information, ideas, and political advice. Cohn had recently gained public prominence as a prosecutor in the espionage case against Julius and Ethel Rosenberg. In his new role, he helped McCarthy conduct investigations into alleged communist influence in government and public life during the Red Scare. The committee’s work and McCarthy’s methods later became associated with the term McCarthyism, but the available sources do not establish that Cohn invented the phenomenon or was its sole architect. They also do not connect this 1953 appointment to Donald Trump, who was born years later. The documented event is Cohn’s hiring and influential role on McCarthy’s committee; the title’s claim of authorship and Trump framing went beyond the historical evidence.
evidence_notes: PBS says McCarthy hired Cohn in 1953 and relied on him for advice and contacts. The source confirms year, not the timeline’s precise January 2 date or claim that Cohn invented McCarthyism.
corrected_wording: Replaced the sweeping authorship claim and irrelevant Trump prefix with the documented appointment and role.

title: Trump Attended Fordham for Two Years Before Transferring to Penn
description_medium: Donald Trump studied economics at Fordham University’s Rose Hill campus in the Bronx for his first two college years, commuting from Queens, then transferred to the University of Pennsylvania and graduated in 1968. Fordham’s student newspaper interviewed classmates and cited a 1965 yearbook listing him as a freshman on the squash team. The supplied account does not establish the timeline’s exact July 1 enrollment date.
description_long: Donald Trump attended Fordham University’s Rose Hill campus in the Bronx for two years before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his degree in 1968. Fordham’s student newspaper reported on the two-year attendance after interviewing more than 60 alumni. Former classmates recalled Trump commuting from Queens, sometimes sharing rides across the Triborough Bridge, and playing sports; the 1965 Maroon yearbook lists him on the freshman squash team. The yearbook provides contemporaneous evidence that he was at Fordham by that academic year, while the interviews supply recollections of daily student life. A TrumpFile timeline assigns the event the date July 1, 1964, but its own note says the exact enrollment date is unknown. The available sources support his attendance and subsequent transfer, not a precise date of enrollment. A separate claim in the timeline that his sister completed homework for him is not substantiated in the linked Fordham account and is omitted.
evidence_notes: Fordham Ram reports interviews with alumni and contemporaneous yearbook evidence; the page notes no university statement. The TrumpFile source itself says the precise enrollment day is unknown.
corrected_wording: Replaced the unsupported exact date and unrelated homework allegation with the supported two-year enrollment, yearbook evidence, and transfer.
exact_blocker: The source material establishes attendance by 1965 but does not verify July 1, 1964 as the enrollment date.

title: Trump Received Four Student Deferments and a Medical Deferment During Vietnam-Era Draft
description_medium: Selective Service records show that Donald Trump received four educational deferments while attending Fordham and the University of Pennsylvania. After graduating in 1968, he received a 1-Y medical deferment, which The New York Times reported followed a diagnosis of heel spurs. The records still available in the National Archives do not identify the condition. The documents establish five deferments, but do not by themselves establish that the diagnosis was fabricated or that Trump deliberately evaded service.
description_long: During the Vietnam-era draft, Donald Trump received four student deferments while studying at Fordham University and the University of Pennsylvania. After graduating in 1968, he received a 1-Y medical deferment. The New York Times reported that Trump said a doctor diagnosed bone spurs in his heels and wrote a letter for his local draft board. Selective Service records obtained from the National Archives do not specify the condition, and Trump could not recall the doctor’s name when asked by the Times. A Selective Service spokesman said Trump was already medically exempted before the 1969 draft lottery, so his eventual lottery number did not determine his status. The medical classification later changed to 4-F in 1972. The records document four education deferments and one medical deferment; they do not prove that the diagnosis was fabricated or establish that Trump’s intent was to evade service. The original headline’s fifth deferment count was accurate, but “dodges” asserted a motive beyond the documentary record.
evidence_notes: NYT/Boston Globe report the five deferments and distinguish Trump’s account of heel spurs from what surviving Selective Service records specify. Avoid asserting the diagnosis was false or that motive is established.
corrected_wording: Preserved the documented five-deferment chronology while changing the title’s unsupported claim of intentional evasion to neutral wording.

title: Trump Executive Order Sought to Gut U.S. Agency for Global Media
description_medium: On March 14, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order aimed at reducing the U.S. Agency for Global Media, which oversees Voice of America and supports Radio Free Asia and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. VOA employees were placed on leave as the administration moved to carry out the order. PEN America said the shutdown endangered journalists and writers who relied on the outlets. A federal court temporarily halted the effort, so the agency’s complete elimination was not established.
description_long: The U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) oversees Voice of America and provides grants to international broadcasters including Radio Free Asia and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. On March 14, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order directing the agency to be reduced to its statutory minimum. VOA employees were placed on leave the next day, and PEN America warned that cuts would undermine reporting and leave journalists working under repressive governments without institutional support. The administration presented the action as a way to eliminate waste and restructure government-funded media. Journalists and unions sued, arguing that the attempt to close USAGM was unlawful. A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order on March 28, blocking the administration from shutting down the agency and requiring steps to restore Voice of America’s operations. These events document a major effort to gut the agency and an immediate operational disruption, followed by court intervention. They do not support a claim that USAGM was eliminated permanently or that all remaining outlets became government propaganda. Later disputes over editorial control require separate evidence.
evidence_notes: The executive order and staffing actions are documented, but the March 28 TRO temporarily blocked shutting the agency down. PEN America represents an advocacy viewpoint on press-freedom consequences; do not state that the full agency or all named networks were permanently eliminated.
corrected_wording: Replaced the claim of completed media transformation with the order, workforce disruption, court injunction, and still-contested status.
exact_blocker: The linked sources do not establish permanent elimination of USAGM or that its outlets were transformed into propaganda operations; the court temporarily blocked closure.

title: Jeffrey Epstein Began Teaching at Dalton as Donald Barr Was Leaving Headmaster Role
description_medium: Jeffrey Epstein began teaching mathematics and physics at Manhattan’s Dalton School in September 1974, several months after headmaster Donald Barr announced he would leave at the end of the school year. The New York Times reported that Barr had made unconventional hires, but a former teacher said it was unclear whether Barr personally hired Epstein. The timeline’s February 15 date refers to Barr’s departure announcement, not Epstein’s appointment.
description_long: Jeffrey Epstein started teaching mathematics and physics at Dalton School in New York in September 1974, despite not having completed college. Donald Barr, father of future Attorney General William Barr, had served as Dalton’s headmaster and announced in February 1974 that he would leave at the end of that school year. A former Dalton teacher told The New York Times that Barr had made unconventional hires, but the article did not establish that Barr personally selected Epstein. The timing of Barr’s announcement and Epstein’s arrival can be documented; it does not by itself establish that Barr hired him or that Barr knew of later misconduct. A TrumpFile timeline labels February 15 as the date Barr hired Epstein, but its own note attributes the hiring claim to former staff, and the dated event appears to be Barr’s resignation announcement rather than Epstein’s September start. The linked reporting describes Epstein’s brief teaching tenure and former students’ recollections of boundary-crossing behavior. It does not establish a connection to Donald Trump or a broader conspiracy involving the Barr family.
evidence_notes: The NYT account reports Epstein started at Dalton in 1974, and a former teacher recalls Barr hiring unconventional staff while saying it is unclear if he hired Epstein. Barr’s February 1974 announcement to leave and Epstein’s September start are distinct events.
corrected_wording: Corrected the event chronology and removed the unproven claim that Barr personally hired Epstein; title now states what the records establish.
exact_blocker: The sources do not establish who at Dalton made Epstein’s appointment, whether Donald Barr personally hired him, or any connection between this personnel decision and Donald Trump.
